entries.appliesTo: the administration of each institution under the Campus Accountability and Safety Act (Louisiana postsecondary institutions)

sources.curriculum: § 3399.16(A), (B)(1) — 'the administration of each institution, in consultation with campus or local law enforcement agencies, shall develop and distribute, not less than four times per academic year through in-person or online delivery or both, information to students regarding power-based violence, campus safety, and internet and cell phone safety' … 'Instruction on … the identification, prevention, dangers, and prohibition of power-based violence and how to detect potential threats to school safety exhibited online, including on any social media platform.'

flags: AI content is definitional only: § 3399.12(5)(b) adds to the 'power-based violence' definition 'Any conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14, or any successor statute, involving media generated by artificial intelligence or deepfake media depicting sexual imagery' — no AI-specific compliance duty is imposed by this act; the criminal prohibitions live in cross-referenced statutes not in this text (rule 4).

Family fit is lossy: bill binds postsecondary institutions ('each institution' under the Campus Accountability and Safety Act, R.S. 17:3399.12 et seq.), but education-k12 is the only education family in the v1.0 vocabulary; no higher-ed family exists.

curriculum coding is lossy: the duty is periodic development and distribution of safety-education information containing 'Instruction on' the listed topics (§ 3399.16(B)(1)), distributed 'not less than four times per academic year', 'as part of new student orientation', and 'posted on an easily accessible page of each institution's website' (§ 3399.16(C)(1)) — a safety-education distribution duty rather than a formal course of study; adjudication chose curriculum over trainingRequired because the text says 'Instruction' to students and the word 'training' appears nowhere in the act.

Minor-student provision: § 3399.16(C)(2) — 'If the student receiving the information required by Subsections B and C of this Section is a minor, the information shall also be provided to his parent or legal guardian.' No matching param in the education-k12 vocabulary.
No penalty or enforcement provision in this text; exposure omitted (silence is silence).
